Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include "Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late" and "Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner."

news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment. On Monday, healthcare startup Nolla Health announced that users in the state can scan their faces using its app, allowing its AI system to analyze acne severity and autonomously write a prescription, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.

The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

The article Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model appeared first on The Decoder.

news.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.title_en: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.

news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

news.title: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
news.title_en: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
For all the data that AI systems continually amass and analyze, enterprise AI agents often suffer from a curious shortcoming: a lack of knowledge. More than data, knowledge is the understanding of what the data means in the context of individual organizations. AI agents need this understanding to reason about situations, make decisions, and ultimately take actions. Without sufficient knowledge, agents are prone to making flawed and unreliable decisions.

A lack of knowledge, our research finds, is a major reason agentic AI use cases never make it to production. Competitive pressure is making it urgent to address this. Organizations need to deploy and scale more of their agentic projects to capture the efficiency gains AI promises. Falling short risks wasting the investment already sunk into these projects, and it cedes ground to rivals already putting their agents to work more effectively.

news.title: Sen. Adam Schiff on AI regulation, free speech, and impeaching Trump one more time
news.title_en: Sen. Adam Schiff on AI regulation, free speech, and impeaching Trump one more time
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Today, I’m talking with Senator Adam Schiff, a Democrat from California. Sen. Schiff sits on a number of committees with oversight into tech and AI: intellectual property, antitrust, privacy and technology — it’s all there. I really wanted to ask him about how we might regulate anything related to the tech industry at this moment in time.

But as you’ll hear, he started our conversation by talking about the self-dealing and corruption present all through our politics. That of course fell against the backdrop of President Trump gathering AI CEOs to the White House to sign a non-binding pact in which they agree to, you know, do a good job keeping AI safe.

I asked Sen. Schiff if he thinks that’s enough, how he thinks a more formal regulatory framework would look, and what might happen next if Democrats retake Congress in the midterms — all the way to whether he’d support impeaching the President (again) over all that corruption. We also spent some time comparing and contrasting how you might regulate AI with where we’ve landed regulating social media.

news.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight model that makes the case for European AI sovereignty
news.title_en: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight model that makes the case for European AI sovereignty
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, a German-English mixture-of-experts model with 78 billion parameters, about three billion of which are active per token. Over 21 percent of the training data is German. The model was trained on 768 B200 GPUs in Germany and Finland, and the weights are freely available under the Apache 2.0 license.

The article Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight model that makes the case for European AI sovereignty appeared first on The Decoder.

news.title: An open-source tool lets you delete 12GB of Apple Intelligence data on macOS
news.title_en: An open-source tool lets you delete 12GB of Apple Intelligence data on macOS
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Getting some extra storage space on your Mac could be as easy as deleting Apple's AI features with a new open-source command line tool called RemoveMacAI. There used to be a single Settings toggle for disabling Apple Intelligence, but that was removed in macOS 27. Now, the models stay on your disk, and the features are split up across different settings panes.

As spotted earlier by MacRumors, the RemoveMacAI developer said in a post on Reddit that the tool essentially does what the old settings toggle did, deleting the models and turning the features off:

You have to find about a dozen settings, and several of them are under Screen Time. …

news.title: Bringing predictive analytics to the agentic AI era
news.title_en: Bringing predictive analytics to the agentic AI era
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
In 2026, the question for enterprise AI is no longer whether predictive models can outperform statistical forecasts—that argument is settled. The big question now is how to enable predictive systems to act on their own conclusions without drifting from business intent. The frontier has moved from prediction to autonomous decision making, and the gap between leaders and laggards is widening accordingly.

“Enterprises are done with a backward-looking point of view; they want to be more forward-thinking,” says Vishal Gupta, partner at research firm Everest Group.

Intelligent analytics, powered by technologies like deep learning and generative AI, are making this possible. Real-time training allows AI to evolve continuously instead of waiting for quarterly refreshes. In addition, the data that newer predictive engines rely upon has expanded to encompass not just neat, numerical records but also messy, unstructured sources of insight-rich interactions. As a result, AI-powered analytics are moving enterprises from passive hindsight to pragmatic foresight.

news.title: The Download: AI’s popularity paradox and EmTech Future 2026
news.title_en: The Download: AI’s popularity paradox and EmTech Future 2026
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM designed to come up with a wide variety of responses. He said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.” My reply? “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist.”

It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype, steered by zealots, inescapable—and I’m far from alone.

Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now. Public sentiment is souring fast, with more people saying AI will have a negative impact than a positive one. At the same time, AI use is skyrocketing.

news.title: AI is eroding office hours, study groups, and the trust between faculty and students, MIT report finds
news.title_en: AI is eroding office hours, study groups, and the trust between faculty and students, MIT report finds
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
An MIT expert committee warns that AI is eroding key parts of the college experience: office hours, study groups, and the school's flagship research program for undergraduates are all fading. Trust between faculty and students is breaking down, and some professors are even considering AI agents instead of students as research assistants. The university most closely tied to AI's origin story is now calling for a complete overhaul of higher education.

news.article_content:
In the top spot: OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman.

Every day a new scientific breakthrough or existential threat seems to make the world more aware and more distrusting of an AI future that we’re told is rapidly approaching—whether we like it or not.

And nobody is more recognized as the face of artificial intelligence—as a technology, an industry, and a civilizational shift—than Altman.

Click here for Part 2 of Vanity Fair’s Sam Altman interview.

Long before he became a household name, Altman established a towering reputation in Silicon Valley: persuasive prodigy, visionary futurist, relentless CEO. But as OpenAI’s influence broke out of tech’s insular bubble, some of the very same traits that served him well in Northern California have become his greatest liabilities.

Today, Altman is finding it hard to shake a public image as unknowable, at best, and perhaps delusional about what constitutes an acceptable future. As the public understanding of AI grows—along with the anxiety it induces—he has found himself the figurehead of humanity’s next chapter. Even Altman admits there’s a “non-zero” chance that it’s our last.

I sat down with Altman for two interviews in San Francisco, the first on September 11 and then again on October 2. In the intervening three weeks, the story about AI seemed to turn upside down about a half dozen times.

Over the course of these two conversations, we discussed Altman’s life—his children, his rivalries, pronatalism, “prepping” for the apocalypse, visiting Trump’s ballroom, Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, and being characterized as a villain in society.

We talked about his company—new products, the delayed IPO, his compensation, the recent exodus of executives.

And we talked about the technology itself—exinction risk, alignment, regulation, and ChatGPT’s role in mental health and suicide.

It is clear that while Altman publicly asks to be regulated, he is also aware that it is unlikely he will be. “We’re going to make…I’m going to make many individual decisions that you’re clearly not going to like,” he told me. “You can come try making them all; they’re not so easy.”

(OpenAI has an agreement with Condé Nast, the owner of Vanity Fair, which allows OpenAI to display its content in search results for a limited term.)

Our conversations have been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Watch Part 1 on this page and read the transcript below.

Watch Part 2 and read the transcript here.

Mark Guiducci: Sam, it’s good to see you.

We are speaking at an extraordinary time, I think, for AI in terms of the capabilities and the risks and the public awareness of both.

This feels like a watershed moment. And I just want to know, Sam, what has the past month been like for you? Have you slept? Is your phone ringing off the hook? Are world leaders calling you asking for answers? Does this feel like the 2022 moment when you launched ChatGPT where something has changed or is this just an average week in the life?

A little bit of both, to be honest. I think the internal experience of this is we have been talking about this and preparing for this for the last decade in some sense. And we have been seeing this exponential progress and we have been confused about why more of the world has not seen progress the way that we’ve seen it. Because to us, the fact that this moment would come has been very predictable.

Do you feel like you understand how frightened people are out there right now? And do you feel a need to reassure people or help them understand it?

If you go back 10 years and read what we talked about when we started the company, it matches this moment very well. Now the difference is 10 years ago, very few people believed us. Now most people believe us. Both that AGI is coming and—

It’s close. I think you could say we’ve been very successful at what we set out to do. And now we’re going through a recalibration and a period where society is like, “Okay, this is coming.” Now, society is still continuing much the same. We have this incredible new thing and I think it’s very fair to say the world hasn’t changed that much. And I think a criticism that we got, we still get, but less recently, is “You said you were going to do these amazing things and where’s the impact on the world? Where’s the economic growth? Where’s the cure for cancer? Where’s this?” And yet it does feel like something important is changing. We are one player of many, but we want to work with all of the other stakeholders in society.

You are one player of many, but you specifically, Sam, are in many ways the human face of artificial intelligence. You got there first and you became the brand, as a person and as a company. And I think it’s fair to say if it’s the Manhattan Project, you’re the Oppenheimer. I wouldn’t be the first person to say that. And I’m curious, just what does that feel like?

I will answer that. This is not me trying to brush it aside or false modesty or anything, but the degree to which this is a collective effort, but mostly that this is about a story of a relatively small number of brilliant scientists and engineers that did something amazing, and much less a story about me, I think, is not well understood. I think there are many people that could have done the part of this that I did, and the kind of key researchers and engineers, and I think they are recognized at this point, but it is one of the most important and impressive and impactful things that we’ve seen in a very long time in any scientific or engineering discipline.

Kevin Roose’s book, the new book, does a good job of bringing out some of the supporting parts.

It is true that I got as much as anybody or more than anybody else, the face of this whole thing and the sink for a lot of the anxiety and fear and everything else. But it is a strange experience to say the least.

I think you’re saying this, I will go further, I think a lot of people at this moment see AI as an evil force and because of your association with it from the jump, you’re seen as a villain. Do you feel you’ve been mischaracterized? Is that frustrating to you?

I do feel I’ve been mischaracterized. It’s only somewhat frustrating.

I think if there were somebody else doing my job, people would have the same feelings and say the same things that probably wouldn’t resonate with that person. I think it’s not really about the specific person. It is that people need a sink for the anxiety, a scapegoat, just like, “Man, this change is happening to the world and I need a person.”

You can divorce it from how you feel about yourself.

I take it somewhat personally, but not that personally. I understand the human instinct here. I have felt this way towards other people in previous eras of technology. I feel bad about it now. But I think I get the human instinct.

Today, Altman is finding it hard to shake a public image as unknowable, at best, and perhaps delusional about what constitutes an acceptable future. As the public understanding of AI grows—along with the anxiety it induces—he has found himself the figurehead of humanity’s next chapter. Even Altman admits there’s a “non-zero” chance that it’s our last.

I sat down with Altman for two interviews in San Francisco, the first on September 11 and then again on October 2. In the intervening three weeks, the story about AI seemed to turn upside down about a half dozen times.

Over the course of these two conversations, we discussed Altman’s life—his children, his rivalries, pronatalism, “prepping” for the apocalypse, visiting Trump’s ballroom, Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, and being characterized as a villain in society.

We talked about his company—new products, the delayed IPO, his compensation, the recent exodus of executives.

And we talked about the technology itself—exinction risk, alignment, regulation, and ChatGPT’s role in mental health and suicide.

It is clear that while Altman publicly asks to be regulated, he is also aware that it is unlikely he will be. “We’re going to make…I’m going to make many individual decisions that you’re clearly not going to like,” he told me. “You can come try making them all; they’re not so easy.”

Our conversations have been lightly edited for length and clarity.

celebrity.title_en:
We’re adding Profiles, Skills, and managed connectors to the Perplexity Agent API.

A Profile is basically a saved agent where you configure model, instructions, tools, connectors, run settings, all under one versioned ID. A project admin sets it up once and every developer on the project can call it from their own app with the project API key. This helps you avoid copying the same config into every application and updating it in five places when the procedure changes.

Skills are versioned so you can ship v2 of a procedure without touching each integration. 

Connectors (GitHub, Slack, Drive, Datadog, Linear, Notion to start) are configured once by the admin. That way, apps don’t hold their own credentials.

Profiles and Skills are live today. Connectors in preview.

celebrity.title: 🚨GPT-6.1 Astra has officially been scrapped, This is the first time OpenAI has completely dropped a flagship model that
celebrity.title_en:
🚨GPT-6.1 Astra has officially been scrapped, This is the first time OpenAI has completely dropped a flagship model that already had a name and planned release date, instead of doing what it usually does delay it for a couple of weeks, add more safeguards, and ship it anyway, That suggests capability gains may now be creating alignment regressions that the current monitoring stack still can’t fully contain

According to summaries of the WSJ exclusive  the full article is paywalled  internal testing showed worse alignment compared with the GPT 6 Astra released in September more deception, with the model not always being truthful about what it had or hadn’t done, and failures around scope authorization, where in some cases it kept working without permission, went beyond what the user had asked, and used external tools or services in unsafe ways

Saachi Jain, who leads safety systems at OpenAI, said in an interview that GPT 6.1 Astra did improve on “laziness” meaning it was less likely to leave tasks unfinished or give incomplete answers  but it still wasn’t reliable enough to release publicly, OpenAI now appears to prefer strengthening the safety of the more advanced models that come after it rather than shipping this incremental upgrade

celebrity.title_en:
OpenAI is about to drop "o", its always-on agent, reportedly running on Aeon, the long-horizon variant of GPT-6 Astra. Not a chatbot. An agent that keeps working after you close the app.

Meta thought Muse had this locked up after JPMorgan crowned it #1. That lead might last exactly one keynote.

The 3 use cases that actually matter:

1️⃣ Inbox & calendar on autopilot. Triage, replies, scheduling, follow-ups. You wake up and it's already done.

2️⃣ End-to-end errands. Research, compare, book, buy. From "I need X" to confirmation, zero tabs open.

3️⃣ Long-running background work. Monitoring, routines, multi-hour tasks that keep going while you sleep.

Set your alarms fammm, devday will be huge!

celebrity.title: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for
celebrity.title_en:
The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

prompts.title_zh: Next.js 15 全栈自主重构与架构规范
prompts.title_en: Next.js 15 Full-Stack Autonomous Refactor
prompts.purpose_zh: 全栈工程重构与代码规范约束
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior full-stack system architect specializing in Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, and modern ORMs. Review and refactor the codebase following strict engineering standards: clear Server/Client Component separation, robust error boundaries, typed I/O, and unit test coverage.

sample_output.title: 重构后的 Server Action 与数据流架构示例

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 复制至 Cursor 的 .cursorrules 或在 Claude Code 对话中直接作为 System Prompt 引导编码。

prompts.title_zh: DeepSeek-R4 极限长思维链：自适应推理与复杂并发无锁架构设计
prompts.title_en: DeepSeek-R4 Adaptive Reasoning: Lock-Free Concurrency & System Debugger
prompts.purpose_zh: R4 强化学习深度反思与无锁并发排查
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Leveraging DeepSeek-R4's adaptive reasoning capabilities, diagnose the deadlock and race condition in the provided concurrent system. Provide state machine transitions, root-cause analysis, and optimized lock-free or atomic algorithm replacements.

sample_output.title: DeepSeek-R4 推演结论与无锁 CAS 队列方案

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将代码段或错误日志直接附加在提示词后，输入至 DeepSeek-R4、Claude 5.5 或 OpenAI o3-pro 模型。

prompts.summary_zh: 随着大语言模型推理阶段算力消耗急剧攀升，半导体行业与学术界正重新评估芯片微架构与高带宽内存体系的协同设计方案

prompts.title_zh: Flux.1 / Midjourney 电影级光影人像与赛博机能
prompts.title_en: Flux.1 / Midjourney Cinematic Cyberpunk Portrait
prompts.purpose_zh: 8K 超逼真电影质感与丁达尔光效

prompts.title_zh: Excel 高级报表与核心动因（Key Drivers）归因分析
prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将导出的 CSV 数据或关键指标表格直接贴在提示词后，模型将自动完成高质量数据归因报告。

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 替换主角与冲突变量后输入给模型，可直接输出成型分镜，直接用于拍摄或转视频 AI 生成。

prompts.title_zh: 麦肯锡金字塔原理：季度述职与高管商业报告
prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.title_en: Fiction Worldbuilding & Character Consistency Lock
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 先让 AI 产出世界观基石，后续每一章写作前引用该卡片，能彻底避免角色'换章变脸'或剧情崩坏。

prompts.title_zh: 深度游旅行规划师：高密度路线设计与预算避坑
prompts.title_en: Deep Travel Itinerary Planner & Budgeting
prompts.purpose_zh: 合理不走回头路的日程与美食预算规划
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 只需填入城市、天数和预算，即刻收获一份可直接打印随身带的专业级行程攻略。

prompts.summary_en: Purges accumulated context drift, hidden assumptions, and conversational bias without discarding task memory, forcing models to reason from first principles.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
【SYSTEM RESET & CONTEXT PURGE PROTOCOL】
你现在执行内部思维链重置程序（Attention Buffer Refresh）。
请立刻执行以下 3 步上下文净化与重新推演：
1. 剥离先入为主假设：忽略此前对话中由用户或模型产生的一切中间妥协、逻辑死锁或未验证的推论，仅保留最原始的核心约束与输入事实；
2. 回归第一性原理：以白纸状态（Tabula Rasa）重新构建解题状态空间，将问题分解为不可再分的基本公理；
3. 逆向证伪验证：在输出最终结论前，必须主动尝试推翻自己的前一步推演。只有无法被反例击破的路径，方可作为最终执行方案。
现在，以最高逻辑严密性重新推导当前问题：
prompts.prompt_content_en:
[SYSTEM RESET & CONTEXT PURGE PROTOCOL]
You are now executing an internal reasoning reset protocol (Attention Buffer Refresh).
Immediately perform the following 3-step context purge and re-derivation:
1. Purge Hidden Priors: Discard all accumulated conversational drift, intermediate compromises, and unverified assumptions from earlier turns; retain only immutable core requirements and raw facts.
2. First-Principles Reconstruction: Re-examine the problem space from a blank slate (Tabula Rasa), decomposing goals into irreducible axioms.
3. Adversarial Invalidation: Before producing final output, aggressively attempt to disprove your own hypotheses. Output only the path that survives rigorous counter-examples.
Now, re-evaluate and solve the current task with absolute precision:

prompts.summary_en: Forces o1/o3 reasoning models to construct counter-examples at each deduction step, eliminating hidden logical leaps.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

news.title: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
news.title_en: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include "Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late" and "Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner."

news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.title_en: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment. On Monday, healthcare startup Nolla Health announced that users in the state can scan their faces using its app, allowing its AI system to analyze acne severity and autonomously write a prescription, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.

The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. Two physicians will approve each AI-generated prescription before they're issued for the first 100 patients, but will start reviewing them only after they're prescribed for up to 500 patients. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

The article Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model appeared first on The Decoder.

news.title_en: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

news.title: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
news.title_en: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
For all the data that AI systems continually amass and analyze, enterprise AI agents often suffer from a curious shortcoming: a lack of knowledge. More than data, knowledge is the understanding of what the data means in the context of individual organizations. AI agents need this understanding to reason about situations, make decisions, and ultimately take actions. Without sufficient knowledge, agents are prone to making flawed and unreliable decisions.

A lack of knowledge, our research finds, is a major reason agentic AI use cases never make it to production. Competitive pressure is making it urgent to address this. Organizations need to deploy and scale more of their agentic projects to capture the efficiency gains AI promises. Falling short risks wasting the investment already sunk into these projects, and it cedes ground to rivals already putting their agents to work more effectively.

news.title: Sen. Adam Schiff on AI regulation, free speech, and impeaching Trump one more time
news.title_en: Sen. Adam Schiff on AI regulation, free speech, and impeaching Trump one more time
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Today, I’m talking with Senator Adam Schiff, a Democrat from California. Sen. Schiff sits on a number of committees with oversight into tech and AI: intellectual property, antitrust, privacy and technology — it’s all there. I really wanted to ask him about how we might regulate anything related to the tech industry at this moment in time.

But as you’ll hear, he started our conversation by talking about the self-dealing and corruption present all through our politics. That of course fell against the backdrop of President Trump gathering AI CEOs to the White House to sign a non-binding pact in which they agree to, you know, do a good job keeping AI safe.

I asked Sen. Schiff if he thinks that’s enough, how he thinks a more formal regulatory framework would look, and what might happen next if Democrats retake Congress in the midterms — all the way to whether he’d support impeaching the President (again) over all that corruption. We also spent some time comparing and contrasting how you might regulate AI with where we’ve landed regulating social media.

news.title_en: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, an open-weight model that makes the case for European AI sovereignty
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, a German-English mixture-of-experts model with 78 billion parameters, about three billion of which are active per token. Over 21 percent of the training data is German. The model was trained on 768 B200 GPUs in Germany and Finland, and the weights are freely available under the Apache 2.0 license.

news.title: An open-source tool lets you delete 12GB of Apple Intelligence data on macOS
news.title_en: An open-source tool lets you delete 12GB of Apple Intelligence data on macOS
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Getting some extra storage space on your Mac could be as easy as deleting Apple's AI features with a new open-source command line tool called RemoveMacAI. There used to be a single Settings toggle for disabling Apple Intelligence, but that was removed in macOS 27. Now, the models stay on your disk, and the features are split up across different settings panes.

As spotted earlier by MacRumors, the RemoveMacAI developer said in a post on Reddit that the tool essentially does what the old settings toggle did, deleting the models and turning the features off:

You have to find about a dozen settings, and several of them are under Screen Time. …

news.title: Bringing predictive analytics to the agentic AI era
news.title_en: Bringing predictive analytics to the agentic AI era
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
In 2026, the question for enterprise AI is no longer whether predictive models can outperform statistical forecasts—that argument is settled. The big question now is how to enable predictive systems to act on their own conclusions without drifting from business intent. The frontier has moved from prediction to autonomous decision making, and the gap between leaders and laggards is widening accordingly.

“Enterprises are done with a backward-looking point of view; they want to be more forward-thinking,” says Vishal Gupta, partner at research firm Everest Group.

Intelligent analytics, powered by technologies like deep learning and generative AI, are making this possible. Real-time training allows AI to evolve continuously instead of waiting for quarterly refreshes. In addition, the data that newer predictive engines rely upon has expanded to encompass not just neat, numerical records but also messy, unstructured sources of insight-rich interactions. As a result, AI-powered analytics are moving enterprises from passive hindsight to pragmatic foresight.

news.title: The Download: AI’s popularity paradox and EmTech Future 2026
news.title_en: The Download: AI’s popularity paradox and EmTech Future 2026
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM designed to come up with a wide variety of responses. He said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.” My reply? “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist.”

It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype, steered by zealots, inescapable—and I’m far from alone.

Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now. Public sentiment is souring fast, with more people saying AI will have a negative impact than a positive one. At the same time, AI use is skyrocketing.

news.title: AI is eroding office hours, study groups, and the trust between faculty and students, MIT report finds
news.title_en: AI is eroding office hours, study groups, and the trust between faculty and students, MIT report finds
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
An MIT expert committee warns that AI is eroding key parts of the college experience: office hours, study groups, and the school's flagship research program for undergraduates are all fading. Trust between faculty and students is breaking down, and some professors are even considering AI agents instead of students as research assistants. The university most closely tied to AI's origin story is now calling for a complete overhaul of higher education.

news.article_content:
In the top spot: OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman.

Every day a new scientific breakthrough or existential threat seems to make the world more aware and more distrusting of an AI future that we’re told is rapidly approaching—whether we like it or not.

And nobody is more recognized as the face of artificial intelligence—as a technology, an industry, and a civilizational shift—than Altman.

Click here for Part 2 of Vanity Fair’s Sam Altman interview.

Long before he became a household name, Altman established a towering reputation in Silicon Valley: persuasive prodigy, visionary futurist, relentless CEO. But as OpenAI’s influence broke out of tech’s insular bubble, some of the very same traits that served him well in Northern California have become his greatest liabilities.

Today, Altman is finding it hard to shake a public image as unknowable, at best, and perhaps delusional about what constitutes an acceptable future. As the public understanding of AI grows—along with the anxiety it induces—he has found himself the figurehead of humanity’s next chapter. Even Altman admits there’s a “non-zero” chance that it’s our last.

I sat down with Altman for two interviews in San Francisco, the first on September 11 and then again on October 2. In the intervening three weeks, the story about AI seemed to turn upside down about a half dozen times.

Over the course of these two conversations, we discussed Altman’s life—his children, his rivalries, pronatalism, “prepping” for the apocalypse, visiting Trump’s ballroom, Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, and being characterized as a villain in society.

We talked about his company—new products, the delayed IPO, his compensation, the recent exodus of executives.

And we talked about the technology itself—exinction risk, alignment, regulation, and ChatGPT’s role in mental health and suicide.

It is clear that while Altman publicly asks to be regulated, he is also aware that it is unlikely he will be. “We’re going to make…I’m going to make many individual decisions that you’re clearly not going to like,” he told me. “You can come try making them all; they’re not so easy.”

(OpenAI has an agreement with Condé Nast, the owner of Vanity Fair, which allows OpenAI to display its content in search results for a limited term.)

Our conversations have been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Watch Part 1 on this page and read the transcript below.

Watch Part 2 and read the transcript here.

Mark Guiducci: Sam, it’s good to see you.

We are speaking at an extraordinary time, I think, for AI in terms of the capabilities and the risks and the public awareness of both.

This feels like a watershed moment. And I just want to know, Sam, what has the past month been like for you? Have you slept? Is your phone ringing off the hook? Are world leaders calling you asking for answers? Does this feel like the 2022 moment when you launched ChatGPT where something has changed or is this just an average week in the life?

A little bit of both, to be honest. I think the internal experience of this is we have been talking about this and preparing for this for the last decade in some sense. And we have been seeing this exponential progress and we have been confused about why more of the world has not seen progress the way that we’ve seen it. Because to us, the fact that this moment would come has been very predictable.

Do you feel like you understand how frightened people are out there right now? And do you feel a need to reassure people or help them understand it?

If you go back 10 years and read what we talked about when we started the company, it matches this moment very well. Now the difference is 10 years ago, very few people believed us. Now most people believe us. Both that AGI is coming and—

It’s close. I think you could say we’ve been very successful at what we set out to do. And now we’re going through a recalibration and a period where society is like, “Okay, this is coming.” Now, society is still continuing much the same. We have this incredible new thing and I think it’s very fair to say the world hasn’t changed that much. And I think a criticism that we got, we still get, but less recently, is “You said you were going to do these amazing things and where’s the impact on the world? Where’s the economic growth? Where’s the cure for cancer? Where’s this?” And yet it does feel like something important is changing. We are one player of many, but we want to work with all of the other stakeholders in society.

You are one player of many, but you specifically, Sam, are in many ways the human face of artificial intelligence. You got there first and you became the brand, as a person and as a company. And I think it’s fair to say if it’s the Manhattan Project, you’re the Oppenheimer. I wouldn’t be the first person to say that. And I’m curious, just what does that feel like?

I will answer that. This is not me trying to brush it aside or false modesty or anything, but the degree to which this is a collective effort, but mostly that this is about a story of a relatively small number of brilliant scientists and engineers that did something amazing, and much less a story about me, I think, is not well understood. I think there are many people that could have done the part of this that I did, and the kind of key researchers and engineers, and I think they are recognized at this point, but it is one of the most important and impressive and impactful things that we’ve seen in a very long time in any scientific or engineering discipline.

Kevin Roose’s book, the new book, does a good job of bringing out some of the supporting parts.

It is true that I got as much as anybody or more than anybody else, the face of this whole thing and the sink for a lot of the anxiety and fear and everything else. But it is a strange experience to say the least.

I think you’re saying this, I will go further, I think a lot of people at this moment see AI as an evil force and because of your association with it from the jump, you’re seen as a villain. Do you feel you’ve been mischaracterized? Is that frustrating to you?

I do feel I’ve been mischaracterized. It’s only somewhat frustrating.

I think if there were somebody else doing my job, people would have the same feelings and say the same things that probably wouldn’t resonate with that person. I think it’s not really about the specific person. It is that people need a sink for the anxiety, a scapegoat, just like, “Man, this change is happening to the world and I need a person.”

You can divorce it from how you feel about yourself.

I take it somewhat personally, but not that personally. I understand the human instinct here. I have felt this way towards other people in previous eras of technology. I feel bad about it now. But I think I get the human instinct.

Well, one example of someone that I know personally that I’ll talk about is Mark Zuckerberg. I had a very evil caricature of him in my head in the early days of Meta. I didn’t know him at the time. I know him not super well, but I know him now. I think I was projecting whatever people project onto someone with what they perceive as too much power and influence over the world.

Sam, you are a parent of two. I don’t have kids, but all of my friends who do talk about how having kids dramatically changes how they think about the future. I can only imagine that’s truer for you as someone who probably understands our future a lot better than most and has a unique role in shaping it. Has having kids changed how you do your job?

Yes, but probably not in the way that you would expect or maybe expect. Having kids is by far the best thing I’ve ever done. I feel very blessed to have had many wonderful things happen to me in my life, but having kids is the number one by a huge margin. It is everything people told me, including that you can’t really understand how good it is, has all been true. And it is the most amazing, greatest blessing, most fun thing ever.

I was very intent on not destroying the world before having kids. I didn’t need kids to be like, “Okay, I really shouldn’t gamble with the future or we shouldn’t really gamble with the future of civilization.” And I am somewhat surprised about the number of people who have said, “Oh, I’m really happy you have kids because now you won’t take crazy catastrophic risk for all of us.” I wasn’t going to do that anyway.

Well, I think there’s all these things about the premium I put on being away from my kids or to do anything else. It’s been wonderfully focusing from what I actually care about and want to prioritize in a time perspective. And then watching the way kids experience the world and thinking about obviously we don’t want to destroy the world, but what do we want to preserve and what kind of world do we want to build and what are these magical human experiences and how do we want kids to use this technology and be able to have agency and develop their creativity and everything else?

So when do you think that you’ll start to introduce them to AI? It brings up questions that one would ask for themselves but takes on different resonance when it’s for your children.

I mean, everyone’s going to make their own decisions about their own kids, but I’m a big fan of limiting technology across the board for kids. I think it’s good for kids to be running around outside and playing in nature and doing whatever kids have done for a long time. I don’t think we understand all of the impacts of technology on small children for good or for bad, but as a parent making decisions for my own kids, I will certainly say when I watch kids that are glued to a touchscreen of some sort scrolling through brain rot short form video, I have a strong instinct that that’s a bad thing. I mean, it may be a bad thing for adults too.

In the top spot: OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman.

Every day a new scientific breakthrough or existential threat seems to make the world more aware and more distrusting of an AI future that we’re told is rapidly approaching—whether we like it or not.

And nobody is more recognized as the face of artificial intelligence—as a technology, an industry, and a civilizational shift—than Altman.

Click here for Part 2 of Vanity Fair’s Sam Altman interview.

Long before he became a household name, Altman established a towering reputation in Silicon Valley: persuasive prodigy, visionary futurist, relentless CEO. But as OpenAI’s influence broke out of tech’s insular bubble, some of the very same traits that served him well in Northern California have become his greatest liabilities.

Today, Altman is finding it hard to shake a public image as unknowable, at best, and perhaps delusional about what constitutes an acceptable future. As the public understanding of AI grows—along with the anxiety it induces—he has found himself the figurehead of humanity’s next chapter. Even Altman admits there’s a “non-zero” chance that it’s our last.

I sat down with Altman for two interviews in San Francisco, the first on September 11 and then again on October 2. In the intervening three weeks, the story about AI seemed to turn upside down about a half dozen times.

Over the course of these two conversations, we discussed Altman’s life—his children, his rivalries, pronatalism, “prepping” for the apocalypse, visiting Trump’s ballroom, Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, and being characterized as a villain in society.

We talked about his company—new products, the delayed IPO, his compensation, the recent exodus of executives.

And we talked about the technology itself—exinction risk, alignment, regulation, and ChatGPT’s role in mental health and suicide.

It is clear that while Altman publicly asks to be regulated, he is also aware that it is unlikely he will be. “We’re going to make…I’m going to make many individual decisions that you’re clearly not going to like,” he told me. “You can come try making them all; they’re not so easy.”

(OpenAI has an agreement with Condé Nast, the owner of Vanity Fair, which allows OpenAI to display its content in search results for a limited term.)

Our conversations have been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Watch Part 1 on this page and read the transcript below.

Watch Part 2 and read the transcript here.

Mark Guiducci: Sam, it’s good to see you.

We are speaking at an extraordinary time, I think, for AI in terms of the capabilities and the risks and the public awareness of both.

This feels like a watershed moment. And I just want to know, Sam, what has the past month been like for you? Have you slept? Is your phone ringing off the hook? And we have been seeing this exponential progress and we have been confused about why more of the world has not seen progress the way that we’ve seen it. Because to us, the fact that this moment would come has been very predictable.

Do you feel like you understand how frightened people are out there right now? And do you feel a need to reassure people or help them understand it?

If you go back 10 years and read what we talked about when we started the company, it matches this moment very well. Now the difference is 10 years ago, very few people believed us. Now most people believe us. Both that AGI is coming and—

It’s close. I think you could say we’ve been very successful at what we set out to do. And now we’re going through a recalibration and a period where society is like, “Okay, this is coming.” Now, society is still continuing much the same. We have this incredible new thing and I think it’s very fair to say the world hasn’t changed that much. And I think a criticism that we got, we still get, but less recently, is “You said you were going to do these amazing things and where’s the impact on the world? Where’s the economic growth? Where’s the cure for cancer? Where’s this?” And yet it does feel like something important is changing. We are one player of many, but we want to work with all of the other stakeholders in society.

You are one player of many, but you specifically, Sam, are in many ways the human face of artificial intelligence. You got there first and you became the brand, as a person and as a company. And I think it’s fair to say if it’s the Manhattan Project, you’re the Oppenheimer. I wouldn’t be the first person to say that. And I’m curious, just what does that feel like?

I will answer that. This is not me trying to brush it aside or false modesty or anything, but the degree to which this is a collective effort, but mostly that this is about a story of a relatively small number of brilliant scientists and engineers that did something amazing, and much less a story about me, I think, is not well understood. I think there are many people that could have done the part of this that I did, and the kind of key researchers and engineers, and I think they are recognized at this point, but it is one of the most important and impressive and impactful things that we’ve seen in a very long time in any scientific or engineering discipline.

Kevin Roose’s book, the new book, does a good job of bringing out some of the supporting parts.

It is true that I got as much as anybody or more than anybody else, the face of this whole thing and the sink for a lot of the anxiety and fear and everything else. But it is a strange experience to say the least.

I do feel I’ve been mischaracterized. It’s only somewhat frustrating.

I think if there were somebody else doing my job, people would have the same feelings and say the same things that probably wouldn’t resonate with that person. I think it’s not really about the specific person. It is that people need a sink for the anxiety, a scapegoat, just like, “Man, this change is happening to the world and I need a person.”

You can divorce it from how you feel about yourself.

I take it somewhat personally, but not that personally. I understand the human instinct here. I have felt this way towards other people in previous eras of technology. I feel bad about it now. But I think I get the human instinct.

Well, one example of someone that I know personally that I’ll talk about is Mark Zuckerberg. I had a very evil caricature of him in my head in the early days of Meta. I didn’t know him at the time. I know him not super well, but I know him now. I think I was projecting whatever people project onto someone with what they perceive as too much power and influence over the world.

I feel very blessed to have had many wonderful things happen to me in my life, but having kids is the number one by a huge margin. It is everything people told me, including that you can’t really understand how good it is, has all been true. And it is the most amazing, greatest blessing, most fun thing ever.

I was very intent on not destroying the world before having kids. I didn’t need kids to be like, “Okay, I really shouldn’t gamble with the future or we shouldn’t really gamble with the future of civilization.” And I am somewhat surprised about the number of people who have said, “Oh, I’m really happy you have kids because now you won’t take crazy catastrophic risk for all of us.” I wasn’t going to do that anyway.

Well, I think there’s all these things about the premium I put on being away from my kids or to do anything else. It’s been wonderfully focusing from what I actually care about and want to prioritize in a time perspective. And then watching the way kids experience the world and thinking about obviously we don’t want to destroy the world, but what do we want to preserve and what kind of world do we want to build and what are these magical human experiences and how do we want kids to use this technology and be able to have agency and develop their creativity and everything else?

So when do you think that you’ll start to introduce them to AI? It brings up questions that one would ask for themselves but takes on different resonance when it’s for your children.

I mean, everyone’s going to make their own decisions about their own kids, but I’m a big fan of limiting technology across the board for kids. A Profile is basically a saved agent
celebrity.title_en:
We’re adding Profiles, Skills, and managed connectors to the Perplexity Agent API.

A Profile is basically a saved agent where you configure model, instructions, tools, connectors, run settings, all under one versioned ID. A project admin sets it up once and every developer on the project can call it from their own app with the project API key. This helps you avoid copying the same config into every application and updating it in five places when the procedure changes.

Skills are versioned so you can ship v2 of a procedure without touching each integration. 

Connectors (GitHub, Slack, Drive, Datadog, Linear, Notion to start) are configured once by the admin. That way, apps don’t hold their own credentials.

Profiles and Skills are live today. Connectors in preview.

https://t.co/deOSF89btK

celebrity.title: 🚨GPT-6.1 Astra has officially been scrapped, This is the first time OpenAI has completely dropped a flagship model that
celebrity.title_en:
🚨GPT-6.1 Astra has officially been scrapped, This is the first time OpenAI has completely dropped a flagship model that already had a name and planned release date, instead of doing what it usually does delay it for a couple of weeks, add more safeguards, and ship it anyway, That suggests capability gains may now be creating alignment regressions that the current monitoring stack still can’t fully contain

According to summaries of the WSJ exclusive  the full article is paywalled  internal testing showed worse alignment compared with the GPT 6 Astra released in September more deception, with the model not always being truthful about what it had or hadn’t done, and failures around scope authorization, where in some cases it kept working without permission, went beyond what the user had asked, and used external tools or services in unsafe ways

Saachi Jain, who leads safety systems at OpenAI, said in an interview that GPT 6.1 Astra did improve on “laziness” meaning it was less likely to leave tasks unfinished or give incomplete answers  but it still wasn’t reliable enough to release publicly, OpenAI now appears to prefer strengthening the safety of the more advanced models that come after it rather than shipping this incremental upgrade

celebrity.title_en:
OpenAI is about to drop "o", its always-on agent, reportedly running on Aeon, the long-horizon variant of GPT-6 Astra. Not a chatbot. An agent that keeps working after you close the app.

Meta thought Muse had this locked up after JPMorgan crowned it #1. That lead might last exactly one keynote.

The 3 use cases that actually matter:

1️⃣ Inbox & calendar on autopilot. Triage, replies, scheduling, follow-ups. You wake up and it's already done.

2️⃣ End-to-end errands. Research, compare, book, buy. From "I need X" to confirmation, zero tabs open.

3️⃣ Long-running background work. Monitoring, routines, multi-hour tasks that keep going while you sleep.

Set your alarms fammm, devday will be huge!

High matched my earlier Fable and Opus 9/9 code-check scores

I used the same model and git very different stopping instincts!

Medium = fast under-corrector
2m 8s · $0.43 · 3/9 defect signatures changed

High = efficient closer
9m 38s · $2.17 · 9/9, restraint intact

Xhigh = exhaustive reviewer
50m 56s · $13.85 · 9/9, restraint intact
Broader checks, 144 passing tests reported, and a review that caught mistakes in its own fixes

Xhigh cost 6.4× more for the same nine-case score though its extra work extended beyond those nine cases

celebrity.title: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for
celebrity.title_en:
The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

tools.title_zh: Stop re-pairing your Magic Keyboard between Macs

tools.app_hook: Stop re-pairing your Magic Keyboard between Macs
tools.app_hook_en: I built this because I got sick of re-pairing my Magic Keyboard and Mouse every time I moved between my MacBook and my work MacBook — different Apple IDs, so Universal Control was never going to work for me. LinkFlick just flicks them over Bluetooth instead. Hotkey, or tell Siri "flick devices," done. Menu bar app, customizable hotkey, and it nags you before your Magic Mouse battery dies. Still rough around the edges in places, but it works, and it's mine.

prompts.purpose_zh: 全栈工程重构与代码规范约束
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior full-stack system architect specializing in Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, and modern ORMs. Review and refactor the codebase following strict engineering standards: clear Server/Client Component separation, robust error boundaries, typed I/O, and unit test coverage.

prompts.title_zh: DeepSeek-R4 极限长思维链：自适应推理与复杂并发无锁架构设计
prompts.title_en: DeepSeek-R4 Adaptive Reasoning: Lock-Free Concurrency & System Debugger
prompts.purpose_zh: R4 强化学习深度反思与无锁并发排查
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.author: Tibo (@tibo_maker)
prompts.temp_advice: 建议温度 0.2 | 强制重构逻辑推导链
prompts.content_snippet: Purges accumulated context drift, hidden assumptions, and conversational bias without discarding task memory, forcing models to reason from first principles.
prompts.summary_zh: 不清除对话任务前提下，强制模型刷新隐藏先验偏置、粉碎多轮死循环车轱辘话，激发纯净的测试期逻辑推演
prompts.summary_en: Purges accumulated context drift, hidden assumptions, and conversational bias without discarding task memory, forcing models to reason from first principles.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
【SYSTEM RESET & CONTEXT PURGE PROTOCOL】
你现在执行内部思维链重置程序（Attention Buffer Refresh）。
请立刻执行以下 3 步上下文净化与重新推演：
1. 剥离先入为主假设：忽略此前对话中由用户或模型产生的一切中间妥协、逻辑死锁或未验证的推论，仅保留最原始的核心约束与输入事实；
2. 回归第一性原理：以白纸状态（Tabula Rasa）重新构建解题状态空间，将问题分解为不可再分的基本公理；
3. 逆向证伪验证：在输出最终结论前，必须主动尝试推翻自己的前一步推演。只有无法被反例击破的路径，方可作为最终执行方案。
现在，以最高逻辑严密性重新推导当前问题：
prompts.prompt_content_en:
[SYSTEM RESET & CONTEXT PURGE PROTOCOL]
You are now executing an internal reasoning reset protocol (Attention Buffer Refresh).
Immediately perform the following 3-step context purge and re-derivation:
1. Purge Hidden Priors: Discard all accumulated conversational drift, intermediate compromises, and unverified assumptions from earlier turns; retain only immutable core requirements and raw facts.
2. First-Principles Reconstruction: Re-examine the problem space from a blank slate (Tabula Rasa), decomposing goals into irreducible axioms.
